# cgjrapp

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrapp/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrapp/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrapp/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrapp)
<!-- badges: end -->

`cgjrapp` is the Shiny dashboard for the institutional chapter of the World
Bank's **Country Jobs and Growth Report (CGJR)**. It benchmarks a country,
region or income group against a chosen comparison group across the CGJR
governance taxonomy, using Closeness-to-Frontier (CTF) indicator data from the
companion [`cgjrdata`](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrdata)
package.

## What it does

- **Sidebar selection.** Pick a base unit and a comparison group — countries,
  WB regions and income groups are all selectable together. Choose the
  benchmarking thresholds (quartiles or terciles) and a year range, then
  *Apply*.
- **Benchmarking tab.** A nested accordion generated from `cgjr_taxonomy`
  (cluster → subcluster → sub-subcluster). Each leaf card shows the base
  unit's indicators against the comparison group, coloured Weak / Emerging /
  Strong, plus a **live composite score**. Static (latest snapshot) or
  Dynamic (over time, even years).
- **Data tab.** Download the live composite scores, the precomputed
  `cgjr_scores` reference (a *different* calculation, labelled as such), the
  indicator-level CTF and raw values, and the full indicator catalogue.
- **AI Report tab.** Draft the governance chapter, or one cluster or
  section of it, following the CGJR guidance note, and ask questions in the
  Chat. Every citation and figure is checked automatically (see below).

Composite scores are **computed live for the chosen comparison group** — a
deliberate port of the CLIAR methodology (`def_quantiles()` /
`compute_family_average_app()`), checked cell-for-cell against `cliarappak`'s
own functions. Indicators the base unit lacks, or that are flat across the
group, are dropped first, so the numbers depend on the selection.

## Prerequisites

`cgjrapp` depends on the `cgjrdata` package (tidy-tibble build):

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrdata@rewrite-tidy-tibble")
```

## Installation

``` r
pak::pak("WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrapp")
```

## Usage

``` r
library(cgjrapp)
run_cgjrapp()
```

## AI Report and Chat

The **AI Report** tab drafts the governance chapter (the full chapter, one
cluster, or one section) following the CGJR guidance note's structure: for
each area, what the data show, why it matters for growth and jobs, and the
questions the country team still has to answer, then possible
recommendations. The **Chat** sub-tab answers questions from the guidance and
the applied selection's data.

Every figure comes from the dashboard's evidence pack and is cited `[E12]`;
every guidance-derived statement cites a passage `[G1.2-3]`. The app then
checks the text itself (`verify_text()`): cited ids must exist, figures must
match the facts they cite, and studies must be in the guidance's reference
list. In the chat, anything from outside the sources has to sit under a
"Beyond the guidance (general knowledge, not verified)" heading. Hover a
citation to see its source.

### Configuring the LLM

The provider is set by environment variables. Put them in your user-level
`~/.Renviron` (never a file inside the repo), or in the Posit Connect
environment panel:

```
CGJR_LLM_BASE_URL=...   # an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
CGJR_LLM_MODEL=...
CGJR_LLM_API_KEY=...
```

For testing, Google Gemini's free tier works through its OpenAI-compatible
endpoint. Create a key at <https://aistudio.google.com/apikey>, then set:

```
CGJR_LLM_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai
CGJR_LLM_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash
CGJR_LLM_API_KEY=<your key>
```

Gemini's free tier has a small daily quota per model (20 requests a day for
the current Flash model in October 2026). A full chapter uses 6 requests,
plus one per chat question; check your usage at <https://ai.dev/rate-limit>.
Brief overloads (HTTP 503) and per-minute limits are retried automatically.
If a run still fails part-way, **Resume** writes only the parts that are
missing.

Switching to WBG mAI means changing these three variables; no code changes
are needed.

### Which guidance the AI uses

The guidance note is **Official Use Only**, so it is never committed, and by
default it is never sent to an LLM. `CGJR_GUIDANCE_SOURCE` controls which
guidance is used:

- `standin` (default): a synthetic stand-in with the same section structure
  (`inst/guidance_standin/`). It is safe with any provider, and the tests use
  it.
- `real`: the guidance note itself. **Use this only with an approved endpoint
  (WBG mAI).** Build its passages once with `data-raw/guidance_passages.R`
  from the PDF in `inst/docs/` (gitignored). The resulting rds is deployed
  with the app from your machine, or you can point `CGJR_GUIDANCE_PATH` at it.

A live smoke test against the configured provider runs only when you ask for
it: `Sys.setenv(CGJR_LLM_LIVE_TEST = "true"); devtools::test(filter = "llm-live")`.

## The taxonomy

Four clusters, 11 subclusters, 14 leaf nodes (Public Financial Management is
the only branching subcluster). The exact names, ordering and nesting are read
from `cgjrdata::cgjr_taxonomy` — nothing is hardcoded in the app, so a change
to the taxonomy is reflected with no code change.

## Development

``` r
devtools::load_all()
devtools::test()
devtools::check()
devtools::build_readme()
```

The methodology parity tests (`tests/testthat/test-utils_family.R`) need a
sibling checkout of
[`cliarappak`](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cliarappak) (or
`CLIARAPPAK_DIR` set); they skip otherwise.
